Fluoroquinolones and Magnesium Interaction: Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium-containing agents to prevent chelation and reduced drug absorption. Monitor therapy closely. 2. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate and Nortriptyline: These agents increase the effects of nortriptyline through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Magnesium Sulfate and Seizure Risk: When using high doses of magnesium sulfate with drugs that lower the seizure threshold, closely monitor for signs of seizures. 4. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate and Ofloxacin: These agents decrease ofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 5. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate and Olanzapine: These agents increase the effects of olanzapine through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Magnesium Sulfate and CNS Depressants: When using higher doses of magnesium sulfate with CNS depressants, closely monitor for evidence of enhanced central nervous system depression. 7. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate and Olmesartan: These agents increase the toxicity of olmesartan. Co-administration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate and Omadacycline: These agents decrease omadacycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Monitor therapy closely. 10. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate and Oxaprozin: These agents increase the toxicity of oxaprozin. Co-administration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may elevate the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate and Paliperidone: These agents increase the toxicity of paliperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 12.
